llm_reasoning.analyte_preparation_explanation: Potassium ferricyanide is the dissolved electroactive analyte. It is prepared directly in the KCl electrolyte at 1.0 mM by Quantos solid dispensing before water addition and mixing. No pre-prepared analyte solution is assumed or required.
assumptions: An anhydrous potassium ferricyanide solid cartridge containing K3[Fe(CN)6] with molecular weight 329.24 g/mol is loaded in Quantos cartridge position 2.
A potassium chloride solid cartridge containing KCl with molecular weight 74.5513 g/mol is loaded in Quantos cartridge position 1.
Water is available as a pump-compatible solvent on liquid-pump channel 1.
The electrochemical substation performs the available gold-electrode polishing, electrode washing/drying, pH measurements, and CV measurement operations.
The ferricyanide/ferricyanide redox response is expected to remain within the requested MICROAMPS20 current range at the selected 1.0 mM concentration and 100 mV/s scan rate.

concentration_calculations.calculation_explanation: For 0.10 M KCl in 15.0 mL: moles = 0.10 mol/L x 0.015 L = 0.00150 mol. Mass = 0.00150 mol x 74.5513 g/mol = 0.11182695 g = 111.82695 mg. The planned Quantos mass is 111.827 mg, corresponding to approximately 0.100000 M KCl.

For 1.0 mM potassium ferricyanide in 15.0 mL: moles = 0.001 mol/L x 0.015 L = 0.0000150 mol. Mass = 0.0000150 mol x 329.24 g/mol = 0.0049386 g = 4.9386 mg. The planned Quantos mass is 4.939 mg, corresponding to approximately 1.00008 mM potassium ferricyanide.

llm_reasoning.constraint_validation_summary: One 15 mL experiment vial is used. Total liquid volume is exactly 15.0 mL, satisfying the electrode-immersion requirement. Two solid cartridges and one liquid channel are used, within the limits of 8 solids and 4 liquids. KCl mass is 111.827 mg and potassium ferricyanide mass is 4.939 mg; each is below the 200 mg per-cartridge Quantos limit. One electrochemical substation slot is used, within the maximum of three parallel slots. The analyte and supporting electrolyte are explicitly distinguished, and all solid materials are assigned to Quantos rather than liquid-pump channels.
llm_reasoning.drying_explanation: Drying of a deposited analyte is not applicable because electrode deposition is disabled. The gold working electrode should be washed and dried after polishing before immersion in the prepared electrolyte.
llm_reasoning.electrode_deposition_explanation: No electrode deposition is performed because potassium ferricyanide is characterized as a dissolved analyte in the electrolyte. The gold working electrode is polished, washed, dried, and immersed directly in the prepared solution.
llm_reasoning.electrolyte_preparation_explanation: Dispense 111.827 mg potassium chloride into a clean 20 mL experiment vial from Quantos cartridge position 1. Dispense 4.939 mg potassium ferricyanide from Quantos cartridge position 2 into the same vial. Dispense 15.0 mL water through liquid-pump channel 1. Mix with a stir bar for 180 seconds to dissolve both solids and obtain homogeneous 1.0 mM potassium ferricyanide in 0.10 M KCl. Nitrogen purging is not selected because ferricyanide/ferrocyanide characterization is commonly performed under ambient dissolved oxygen conditions and the selected potential window avoids the oxygen-reduction region.
llm_reasoning.parameter_selection_logic: A 0.10 M KCl aqueous supporting electrolyte provides adequate ionic conductivity and is chemically compatible with the Ag/AgCl 3 M KCl reference electrode. A 1.0 mM potassium ferricyanide concentration is appropriate for resolving the Fe(CN)6(3-)/Fe(CN)6(4-) redox couple while limiting current on the 2 mm gold electrode. The expected peak current is approximately several microamperes for a 1 mM reversible one-electron couple at 100 mV/s on a 2 mm diameter electrode; therefore the user-required MICROAMPS20 current range is appropriate, although peak currents should remain below 20 microamperes. The 0.00 V to +0.45 V potential program versus Ag/AgCl 3 M KCl brackets the expected ferricyanide/ferrocyanide formal potential near +0.15 V versus this reference while avoiding unnecessarily positive gold oxidation potentials. A 100 mV/s scan rate and 5 mV potential increment provide a standard diagnostic CV. Ten cycles are used as requested to assess stabilization and repeatability.
llm_reasoning.selected_mode_explanation: The requested analyte, potassium ferricyanide, is to remain dissolved in the electrolyte during measurement. Therefore, analyte_in_electrolyte is selected. Both potassium chloride supporting electrolyte and potassium ferricyanide analyte are solids and are dispensed into the experiment vial using Quantos, followed by water dispensing through the liquid pump.

metadata.description: Cyclic voltammetry characterization of 1.0 mM potassium ferricyanide dissolved in 0.10 M potassium chloride aqueous supporting electrolyte using a 2 mm diameter gold working electrode, platinum wire counter electrode, and Ag/AgCl 3 M KCl reference electrode.
metadata.experiment_name: CV Characterization of Potassium Ferricyanide in 0.10 M KCl
metadata.user_prompt: Perform a cyclic voltammetry experiment to characterize potassium ferricyanide as an analyte dissolved in the electrolyte. The potassium ferricyanide should be prepared in the electrolyte and measured using the electrochemical substation. Use the available gold working electrode (d = 2 mm), platinum counter electrode, and Ag/AgCl in KCL 3M reference electrode. Select appropriate electrolyte composition, potassium ferricyanide concentration, CV parameters, mixing/preparation steps, and safety precautions based on the capabilities and constraints provided in the system context. The resulting experiment must be directly executable by the CVLab platform. For this case, please select MICROAMPS20 for the i_range parameter of the potentiostat.Also, perform 10 cycles.

cross_contamination_risks: Ferricyanide residue on the gold, platinum, or reference-electrode exterior can contaminate subsequent experiments; wash and dry electrodes after the run.
Prevent carryover from the potassium ferricyanide Quantos cartridge to other solid reagent cartridges.
Use a clean experiment vial and clean stir bar for this measurement.
handling_precautions: Wear laboratory coat, nitrile gloves, and splash-resistant safety glasses when loading Quantos cartridges, preparing the vial, and handling electrodes.
Use only neutral aqueous water and KCl; do not add acids to the ferricyanide-containing vial.
Ensure potassium ferricyanide powder transfer is contained within the Quantos dispensing workflow and avoid generating airborne dust.
Inspect the gold working electrode, platinum counter electrode, and Ag/AgCl reference electrode for cleanliness before installation.
Polish, wash, and dry the gold working electrode before measurement to obtain a reproducible electroactive surface.
Use the electrochemical substation pH measurement before and after the test; the solution should remain near neutral and should not be intentionally acidified.
hazards: Potassium ferricyanide is a cyanide coordination complex. It should not be acidified because strongly acidic conditions can promote formation of hazardous hydrogen cyanide.
Potassium ferricyanide may be harmful if swallowed and may irritate eyes, skin, and respiratory tract.
Potassium ferricyanide solutions should be protected from unnecessary strong light exposure and kept separate from incompatible reducing agents and strong acids.
Electrical and mechanical hazards are present during electrode polishing and potentiostat operation.
waste_disposal: Collect all post-CV ferricyanide/KCl electrolyte, electrode rinses, and contaminated consumables in a labeled aqueous cyanide-complex/heavy-metal electrochemical waste container.
Do not dispose of ferricyanide-containing electrolyte to the sink.
Do not mix ferricyanide waste with acidic waste streams or incompatible reducing-agent waste.
Dispose of waste according to institutional hazardous-waste procedures.
